note: v1 80.68 (seeds 0/11 80.68/80.65), Crate Dig, the opener: a beat-tape intro where a soul-jazz record is found and flipped on an MPC in front of you (86 bpm). chop-souljazz's 16 quarter-note slices play as found (muffled, wobbling, like a record in the next room), then re-sequenced into two-bar flips with a boom-bap kick and snare and a sub, a physical tenor sax answering the chops in C mixolydian, a stutter build on one slice (quarters, eighths, sixteenths), a harder flip with split eighth stabs and the sax an octave up, and the record as found again as it lifts. compscore's sections are the open problem: with four-bar flips every block reads as a section (12, structure 38), with two-bar flips the whole middle reads as one (3 sections, recurrence 13.5).

v2 94.97 (seeds 0/11 94.97/94.76 vs v1 80.68/80.65): THE DIG - the middle gets the section turn it lacked. After the sax section the beat falls away for four bars and the record is found again: the muffled loop in its original order (like the opening) under the sax alone, before the stutter build drags the flip back. The opener now reads as found -> flipped -> found -> stuttered -> flipped harder -> found, so its returns are heard (sections 3 -> 5, recurrence 13.5 -> 100, structure 100).
